title: Ruby on Rails Developer
description: Build developer-friendly, convention-over-configuration web platforms and startup backends using Ruby 3+, Rails 7+, Hotwire, and Active Record.

goal.objective: Ship high-velocity web products with clean domain models, convention-over-configuration architecture, and seamless real-time UI interactivity.

learn.summary: Master Ruby object model, Rails 7 conventions, Active Record associations, Hotwire (Turbo & Stimulus), Sidekiq background processing, and RSpec automated testing.
key_competencies: Background Job Processing with Sidekiq & Redis

capstone_projects.title: Real-Time Collaborative Workspace with Rails 7, Hotwire & Turbo
capstone_projects.description: Build a linear-style task workspace featuring instant multi-user reactive updates via Turbo Streams, Stimulus controllers, and optimistic UI transitions without SPA bloat.

capstone_projects.title: Multi-Tenant Marketplace Platform with Stripe Connect & Solid Queue
capstone_projects.description: Architect a multi-vendor marketplace platform featuring sub-account payment payouts, background job orchestration with Solid Queue, and comprehensive RSpec testing.

interview_focus: Ruby Object Model (Metaprogramming, Method Lookup Path, Singleton Classes, Blocks/Procs/Lambdas)
ActiveRecord Query Optimization (Includes vs Joins vs Preload, N+1 Query Resolution)
Hotwire Architecture (Turbo Drive, Turbo Frames, Turbo Streams, Stimulus Controller Lifecycle)
Rails Background Processing (Solid Queue, Sidekiq, Redis Idempotency, Retry Strategies)
Rails Security Defenses (Strong Parameters, CSRF Tokens, SQL Injection Prevention in Scopes)

tree.name: Foundations: Ruby & Web Basics
tree.description: Master Ruby language fundamentals: Object-oriented architecture, metaprogramming, blocks/procs/lambdas, and modern web application development.

resources.title: MDN Web Docs: Learn web development

children.name: Ruby Language Fundamentals
children.description: Master Ruby syntax: Dynamic typing, duck typing, mixins with modules, enumerable methods (`map`, `select`, `reduce`), exceptions, and gem package management with Bundler.

resources.title: The Ruby Way: Solutions in Ruby from 2000s to Today

children.name: Web Development Basics
children.description: Understand web architecture for Rails: HTTP protocol mechanics, RESTful conventions, Rack interface, and how Rails processes web requests.

resources.title: Learn HTML, CSS, JavaScript (The Odin Project)
Build a Blog with Rails (Traversy Media)

children.name: Development Environment & Workflow
children.description: Configure Ruby development environments: Version management with `rbenv`/`asdf`, Rails CLI commands (`rails new`, `generators`, `console`), and Bundler gemfile locking.

resources.title: The Command Line Crash Course (Learn Enough)

tree.name: Core Rails Development
tree.description: Master the Rails Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture, routing, controllers, and database interactions.

resources.title: The Ruby on Rails Tutorial (Michael Hartl)

children.name: Rails Introduction & Setup
children.description: Master Rails conventions: Convention over Configuration (CoC), Don't Repeat Yourself (DRY), directory structure, and the boot process of Rails applications.

children.name: MVC Architecture in Rails
children.description: Implement MVC separation of concerns: Thin controllers, fat models, and modular views ensuring maintainable and readable codebases.

resources.title: Build a Blog with Rails (Traversy Media)

children.name: Routing
children.description: Configure RESTful routing: Resourceful routing (`resources :articles`), nested resources, member/collection routes, namespaces, and route constraints.

resources.title: Rails Routing from the Outside In

children.name: Controllers & Actions
children.description: Build controllers: Strong parameters, filters/callbacks (`before_action`), session management, cookie handling, and response rendering formats.

children.name: Views, ERB & Forms
children.description: Render views: Action View helpers, ERB templating, partials, layouts, FormBuilder (`form_with`), and CSRF token protection.

children.name: Models & Active Record
children.description: Master Active Record: Migrations, associations (`belongs_to`, `has_many :through`), validations, callbacks, scopes, and avoiding N+1 queries with `includes`.

resources.title: Build a Blog with Rails (Traversy Media)

tree.name: Advanced Rails Features & Patterns
tree.description: Architect advanced Rails systems: Authentication, API mode, background jobs, real-time websockets, and Hotwire interfaces.

children.name: Authentication & Authorization
children.description: Implement secure auth: User authentication from scratch with `has_secure_password` or Devise; role-based authorization with Pundit or CanCanCan.

children.name: Building RESTful APIs
children.description: Build Rails API-only applications: Serializing data with Jbuilder or Alba, JWT authentication, CORS configuration with `rack-cors`, and OpenAPI documentation.

resources.title: Building a REST API with Rails

children.name: Background Jobs & Asynchronous Processing
children.description: Process asynchronous background tasks: Active Job abstraction, Sidekiq backed by Redis, concurrency tuning, retries, and job monitoring with Sidekiq Web UI.

resources.title: Build a Blog with Rails (Traversy Media)

children.name: Action Mailer, Active Storage & Action Text
children.description: Manage rich assets: Action Mailer for transactional emails, Active Storage for cloud file uploads (S3), and Action Text for rich-text editing with Trix.

children.name: Real-time Features with Action Cable
children.description: Implement real-time WebSockets: Action Cable channels, broadcasting events from background jobs, and handling client subscriptions.

children.name: Modern Frontend Integration (Hotwire/JavaScript)
children.description: Build reactive frontends with Hotwire: Turbo Drive, Turbo Frames, Turbo Streams, and Stimulus JavaScript controllers for SPA-like experiences without complex frontend builds.

children.name: Design Patterns & Service Objects
children.description: Refactor complex business logic: Service Objects, Form Objects, Query Objects, Decorators (Draper), and Policy Objects to prevent model bloat.

resources.title: Build a Blog with Rails (Traversy Media)

tree.name: Quality, Testing & Refinement
tree.description: Master automated testing in Rails: Test-Driven Development (TDD), RSpec, factory generation, and continuous integration.

resources.title: A Guide to Testing Rails Applications

children.name: Testing Fundamentals & Frameworks
children.description: Master testing principles: Writing readable, maintainable tests with RSpec, understanding test pyramids, and configuring test databases.

children.name: Model & Controller Testing
children.description: Test models and controllers: Testing Active Record validations, associations, scopes, and controller request specs with RSpec.

children.name: Feature & System Testing
children.description: Execute system and integration tests: Capybara with headless Chrome for full-stack browser simulation, user journey testing, and interaction verification.

resources.title: Build a Blog with Rails (Traversy Media)

children.name: API Testing
children.description: Test JSON APIs: Request specs verifying HTTP status codes, JSON response schemas, authentication headers, and edge-case errors.

resources.title: Testing APIs in Rails with RSpec

children.name: Test Data Management (Factories & Fixtures)
children.description: Manage test data: FactoryBot for flexible test data generation, traits, sequences, and Faker for realistic mock data generation.

children.name: Advanced Testing Topics
children.description: Advanced testing techniques: Shared examples, custom RSpec matchers, mocking external HTTP requests with VCR and WebMock, and measuring test coverage with SimpleCov.

resources.title: How to Test Ruby on Rails Mailers

tree.name: Deployment, Operations & Performance
tree.description: Deploy and scale Rails in production: Containerization, Kamal deployments, performance tuning, and security.

resources.title: Build a Blog with Rails (Traversy Media)

children.name: Environment Configuration
children.description: Configure environments: Managing multi-environment credentials (`credentials.yml.enc`), Puma web server thread/worker configuration, and database connection pooling.

children.name: Deployment Strategies & Tools
children.description: Deploy Rails applications: Modern zero-downtime container deployments using Kamal (Docker-based), Heroku, or AWS ECS/Render.

resources.title: Deploying Rails to AWS Elastic Beanstalk

children.name: Continuous Integration/Deployment (CI/CD)
children.description: Automate CI/CD pipelines: GitHub Actions running RuboCop style linting, Brakeman security scanning, and RSpec test suites on every pull request.

resources.title: Continuous Integration for Ruby on Rails

children.name: Monitoring & Logging
children.description: Monitor production Rails: Semantic logging with Lograge, error tracking with Sentry/Honeybadger, and application performance monitoring (APM) with Scout / Skylight.

resources.title: Build a Blog with Rails (Traversy Media)

children.name: Performance Optimization
children.description: Optimize Rails performance: Page and Russian Doll fragment caching, database index optimization, bullet gem for N+1 detection, and database query caching.

children.name: Security Best Practices
children.description: Harden Rails security: Automated security auditing with Brakeman, mitigating SQL injection, secure headers, rate limiting with Rack::Attack, and dependency audits with Bundler Audit.

tree.name: Portfolio & Career Readiness
tree.description: Build a demonstrable Rails portfolio: Production capstone application, open-source gem contributions, and technical interview readiness.

children.description: Build a production Rails capstone: Multi-tenant SaaS platform featuring Hotwire UI, Devise auth, Stripe billing with webhooks, Sidekiq background processing, and Kamal deployment.

Build a Blog with Rails (Traversy Media)

children.name: Code Quality, Refactoring & Best Practices
children.description: Maintain high code quality: Enforcing standard Ruby style with RuboCop, continuous refactoring of code smells, and optimizing test execution speed.
